verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents user control over resource lifecycle: you can destroy Machines directly, run disposable per-request VMs that share no state, and throw away unneeded checkpoints. Together these give glancing, infrastructure-level deletion control, but no explicit data-retention policy or deletion guarantees. One community report says an account-deletion request went unanswered, which lowers confidence but does not contradict a documented vendor claim. Missing for 10: configurable retention periods (e.g., for backups, logs, or checkpoints), documented data/account deletion guarantees or processes, and independent corroboration that deletion works as expected.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: You can create and destroy Machines directly, and you have control over every Machine’s lifecycle, resources, and region placement.
A clean baseline per request, so no two users ever share state. Egress-locked and disposable.
Checkpoint what works, throw away the rest.
